S.TRANSL: "I'd like to take a wife, Mother."

S.FORM: "kaʔanə=pa kau=pa-i mu-sətəa cainana=musu. aranai ʔinia ma-ka-cəkəna ʔani-ʔacaŋə vəkəsə=su."
S.PHON: kaʔanəpa kaupai musətəa ʦainanamusu aranai ʔinia makaʦəkəna ʔaniʔaʦaŋə vəkəsəsu
S.FORM: "ka'anepa kaupai musetea cainanamusu. aranai 'inia makacekena 'ani'acange vekesesu."
S.PHON: kaʔanepa kaupai musetea ʦainanamusu a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia makaʦekena ʔaniʔaʦaŋe vekesesu
S.TRANSL: "You're not old enough yet. (Wait until) your hair reaches your shoulders."

S.PHON: makaʦəkənakani ʔaniʔaʦaŋini vəkəʂini kaʔanəpaku muruʔuʦaŋə tʂina
makaʦekenakani ʔaniʔaʦaŋini vekeʂini kaʔanepaku mu[r|ɾ]uʔuʦaŋe tʂina
S.TRANSL: His hair reached his shoulders (and asked), "Can't I take a wife, Mother?"

S.PHON: makaʦəkəna paʔi na kəkəmusu vəkəsəsu muruʔuʦaŋəʦuʔai
makaʦekena paʔi na kekemusu vekesesu mu[r|ɾ]uʔuʦaŋeʦuʔai
S.TRANSL: (Wait until) your hair reaches your legs before you can take a wife."
"I'd like to take a wife," he said.
"You are not taking a wife yet," she said to him.
He got angry, picked up a spear, went outside.

S.PHON: ʦoomainikasu ʦuuɾu tʂina ʦuməʦəʔəra paaʔi ʔikua
ʦoomainikasu ʦuu[r|ɾ]u tʂina ʦumeʦeʔe[r|ɾ]a paaʔi ʔikua
S.TRANSL: "You really deserve it, Mother. You will not see me any more."

S.FORM: ala-i ʔinia paŋarə mata-cəkəcəkə ta-ta-piniŋ-a, mu-ciri.
S.PHON: aɾai ʔinia paŋarə mataʦəkəʦəkə tatapiniŋa mutʂiri
a[r|ɾ]ai ʔinia paŋa[r|ɾ]e mataʦekeʦeke tatapiniŋa mutʂi[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: He took the spear, planting it (into the ground) outside, and stood there.
Blades of grass grew at his feet.

S.FORM: ʔalikun-au vai=aku, kainu, pu-puta mu-usa=ku cakəranə.
S.PHON: ʔaɾikunau vaiaku kainu puputa muusaku ʦakəranə
ʔa[r|ɾ]ikunau vaiaku kainu puputa muusaku ʦake[r|ɾ]ane
S.TRANSL: Have pity on me, mother Kainu, I went to the river everyday.

S.FORM: tapianaŋai ma-ka-naanu si tia=makai maamia na=ʔiipi=musu?
S.PHON: tapianaŋai makanaanu ʂi tiamakai maamia naʔiipimusu
S.FORM: tapianangai makanaanu si tiamakai maamia na'iipimusu?
S.PHON: tapianaŋai makanaanu ʂi tiamakai maamia naʔiipimusu
S.TRANSL: What kind of bird sounds just like the voice of your late son, 'iipi?

S.FORM: tanirərə-ʔau=pa=kia si ʔaisi=pa=ʔai miana si tia=na=ʔiipi=maku.
S.PHON: tanirərəʔaupakia ʂi ʔaiʂipaʔai miana ʂi tianaʔiipimaku
tani[r|ɾ]e[r|ɾ]eʔaupakia ʂi ʔaiʂipaʔai miana ʂi tianaʔiipimaku
S.TRANSL: I am still consoled because my late son 'iipi seems to be still around.
